questions: If a CSV file contains the target value in the first cell of multiple rows, does the function return the index of the first occurrence only, or should it return the index of the last occurrence or all occurrences?
Should the function handle CSV files with varying delimiters (e.g., tab, semicolon) or assume comma-delimited?
What should happen if the processed_dir does not exist? Should it be created automatically or raise an error?
If a file has already been processed (i.e., moved to processed_dir in a previous run), should it be skipped entirely? How is 'already processed' defined?
Should the function read CSV files recursively in subdirectories of csv_dir, or only directly in the given directory?
What encoding should be used when opening CSV files (e.g., UTF-8, ASCII, system default)?
If a CSV file has no rows (empty) or only a header row, should it be included in the result dictionary with a special value (e.g., None or -1) or omitted?
Should the function handle CSV files where the first cell has leading/trailing whitespace around the target value?
